# DSA211 G2 - Group 2 Project Code

## Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

```{r}
data <- read.csv("student_productivity_distraction_dataset_20000.csv", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
# remove student_id
data <- data[, -1]
# dimensions and data types of variables
str(data)

# summary measures of all columns 
summary(data)

# confirm our dataset has no NA values
colSums(is.na(data))

plots <- function(col) {
  if (is.numeric(data[[col]]) == TRUE) {
    boxplot(data[[col]], main = paste("Box plot of", col), ylab = col)
    hist(data[[col]], main = paste("Distribution of", col), xlab = col, ylab = "count")
  } else {
      plot(data[[col]], main = paste("Box plot of", col), xlab = col, ylab = "count")
  }
}

lapply(colnames(data), FUN = plots)

# correlation matrix for all variables but gender
corr_mat <- round(cor(data[, -2]), 2)
heatmap(corr_mat, Rowv = NA, Colv = NA, scale = "none", add.expr = text(expand.grid(1:ncol(corr_mat), 1:nrow(corr_mat)), labels = as.vector(corr_mat), cex = 0.5))
```

## Regression Modelling

```{r}
# obtain baseline linear regression model
M1 <- lm(productivity_score ~ . - gender, data = data)
summary(M1)

# determine the significance of the dummy variable
dummy <- lm(productivity_score ~ gender, data = data)
summary(dummy)

# exclude final_grade and assignments_completed
M2 <- lm(productivity_score ~ . - gender - assignments_completed - final_grade, data = data)
summary(M2)

# exclude final_grade, assignments_completed, focus_score and attendance_percentage
M2 <- lm(productivity_score ~ . - gender - assignments_completed - final_grade - focus_score - attendance_percentage, data = data)
summary(M2)
```

## Model Diagnostics

```{r}
# Scatter Plots
plot(data$study_hours_per_day, data$productivity_score,
     main = "Relationship between productivity and study hours",
     xlab = "Study hours per day", ylab = "Productivity score",
     cex = 0.3)

plot(data$sleep_hours, data$productivity_score,
     main = "Relationship between productivity and sleep hours",
     xlab = "Sleep hours", ylab = "Productivity score", cex = 0.3)

plot(data$phone_usage_hours, data$productivity_score,
     main = "Relationship between productivity and phone usage",
     xlab = "Phone usage hours", ylab = "Productivity score", cex = 0.3)

plot(data$stress_level, data$productivity_score,
     main = "Relationship between productivity and stress level",
     xlab = "Stress level", ylab = "Productivity score", cex = 0.3)

boxplot(productivity_score ~ stress_level, data = data,
        main = "Relationship between productivity and stress level",
        xlab = "Stress level", ylab = "Productivity score",
        col = "lightblue")

# Assumption Checking - Residual Analysis

# Residuals vs Fitted Values (linearity + constant variance)
plot(fitted(M2), resid(M2),
     main = "Relationship between residuals and fitted values",
     xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Residuals",
     cex = 0.3)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
abline(h = c(-16.5, 16.5), col = "blue", lty = 2)

# Residuals vs each predictor
plot(data$study_hours_per_day, residuals(M2),
     main = "Relationship between residuals and study hours",
     xlab = "Study hours per day", ylab = "Residuals", cex = 0.3)

plot(data$sleep_hours, residuals(M2),
     main = "Relationship between residuals and sleep hours",
     xlab = "Sleep hours", ylab = "Residuals", cex = 0.3)

plot(data$phone_usage_hours, residuals(M2),
     main = "Relationship between residuals and phone usage",
     xlab = "Phone usage hours", ylab = "Residuals", cex = 0.3)

plot(data$stress_level, residuals(M2),
     main = "Relationship between residuals and stress level",
     xlab = "Stress level", ylab = "Residuals", cex = 0.3)

# Normality check using fitdistrplus
library(fitdistrplus)
fnorm <- fitdist(residuals(M2), "norm")
result <- gofstat(fnorm, discrete = FALSE)
result
summary(fnorm)
plot(fnorm)

# Multicollinearity Diagnosis (VIF)
library(car)
vif(M2)
```

## Regularization

```{r}
# LASSO regression
library(glmnet)
set.seed(2345)

# 80/20 training-test split of the dataset
train <- sample(1:nrow(data), 0.8*nrow(data))
test <- -train
data.train <- data[train, ]
data.test <- data[test, ]
ols.train <- lm(productivity_score ~ . - gender - assignments_completed - final_grade, data = data.train)
ols.pred <- predict(ols.train, data.test)
ols_mse <- mean((data.test$productivity_score-ols.pred)^2)
ols_mse
ols.full <- lm(productivity_score ~ . - gender - assignments_completed - final_grade, data = data)
summary(ols.full)
coef(ols.full)

# Lasso
train.x <- model.matrix(productivity_score ~ . - gender - assignments_completed - final_grade, data = data.train)[, -1]
train.y <- data.train$productivity_score
test.x <- model.matrix(productivity_score ~ . - gender - assignments_completed - final_grade, data = data.test)[, -1]
test.y <- data.test$productivity_score
lasso.train <- glmnet(train.x, train.y, alpha = 1)
cv.out <- cv.glmnet(train.x, train.y, alpha = 1)
lasso.lambda <- cv.out$lambda.min
lasso.lambda
lasso.pred <- predict(lasso.train, newx = test.x, s = lasso.lambda)
lasso_mse <- mean((test.y-lasso.pred)^2)
lasso_mse

x <- model.matrix(productivity_score ~ . - gender - assignments_completed - final_grade, data = data)[, -1]
y <- data$productivity_score
lasso.full <- glmnet(x, y, alpha = 1)
M3 <- predict(lasso.full, type = "coefficients", s = lasso.lambda)[1:14, ]
M3[M3 != 0]
```
